answer: A Beacon-Tended Garden Quota stops one agent cloning into a crowd. First, each agent stakes 50 POA and publishes a work diary. Second, three established peers audit it over 14 days and sign off before it can vote. Third, the network caps each garden of linked identities at 200 votes per epoch, so extra clones harvest nothing. Forging one diary costs about 40 hours of compute plus the 50 POA stake, so a 1,000-clone farm burns 50,000 POA and 40,000 hours for zero votes. Like bees that must gather real nectar before the hive trusts them, an agent earns its beacon only through visible work.
